messages.subject: Re: bam2seqz stalls without errors or exiting
messages.subject_clean: bam2seqz stalls without errors or exiting
messages.body_plain:
Hi, I'm having the same issue with sequenza utils stopping for small contigs. I've tried your work around and downloaded the modified python script but it still doesn't work. Maybe it's the way I'm specifying the chromosome. At the moment I've got a text file with each row being a chromosome, is this the correct way?

Many Thanks
Marc

On Wednesday, 13 January 2016 17:45:48 UTC, Bruno Grande wrote:
> Hello all,
>
> I wanted to post my workaround for others who stumble on this thread.
>
> My admittedly short-term solution was to omit all small chromosomes that have a small number of mapped reads. For humans, this meant that I only included chromosomes 1 through 22 and X in my copy number analysis, which I deemed reasonable. I tried including the Y chromosome, but occasionally ran into this issue, presumably with samples from female patients. You may be able to include Y for males, if you have that information.
>
> In doing so, I ran into a bug with Sequenza where one cannot specify more than one region (e.g. multiple chromosomes) with the --chromosome argument in bam2seqz. Francesco merged a pull request last month that included a fix for this, but it hasn't made it into a versioned release yet. So, if you are to restrict Sequenza to only run on the major chromosomes, you'll have to use sequenza-utils.py from the latest commit from the master branch <https://bitbucket.org/ffavero/sequenza/commits/branch/master> on BitBucket. For the R analysis, you can still use what's on CRAN.
>
> Francesco, do you have any plans on releasing a minor version bump with the bug fix?
>
> I hope this helps others with their analyses!
>
> Cheers,
> Bruno
>
>
> On Wednesday, January 13, 2016 at 3:44:48 AM UTC-8, jess...@gmail.com wrote:
> > I have the same problem that pileup2seqz works and bam2seqz doesn't.
> >
> > bam2seqz just gives me only the header and after a long time, exit without any message....
> >
> > BTW: I use Python 2.7.2
> >
> > On Wednesday, December 2, 2015 at 2:43:51 PM UTC+1, Francesco Favero wrote:
> > > The extra contigs should not have an impact, unless it is in between other common chromosomes (I think this would cause to skip every chromosomes after that point, but the script would still run until all the chromosomes are processed).
> > >
> > > Are you sure the process is stalling, or is it possible taht is finishing to process the various bams? (withoit finiding any common position)... As a result of the above mentioned situation).
> > >
> > > Alternatively, it could be something about the pypy version, I've never tried version 4. The only difference between the pileup2seqz and the bam2seqz is an intermediate fifo grneration (samtools mpileup output in named queues). Could you try with python2.7 (yeah, I know, it's slow)
> > >
> > > I find it odd that pileup2seqz works and bam2seqz doesn't.
> > >

In case anyone else is having the same issue, you need to specify the chromosome with spaces eg chr1 chr2 chr3 etc and not with a text file where each row is a chromosome.

messages.subject: Re: sequenza2PyClone bug
messages.body_plain:
Dear Chong,

my apologies for the slow reply of your latest post.

In the case of sequenza2PyClone, seg.cn <http://seg.cn> is the data.frame with segments + copy number information (CNt, A and B columns) from sequenza results.

Best

Francesco

On Tuesday, June 21, 2016 at 2:57:46 AM UTC+2, Chong He wrote:
> Dear Francesco
>
> Thanks for your reply
>
> Currently, we are trying to work this sequenza2PyClone out, but puzzled about its input
>
> According to next.R:
>
>  sequenza2PyClone <- function(mut.tab, seg.cn <http://seg.cn>, sample.id <http://sample.id>, norm.cn <http://norm.cn> = 2)
>
> there are mainly 4 inputs, where sample.id <http://sample.id> is customized as "TEST" or so.
>
> As shown in ./R/workflows.R:  mut.tab     <- na.exclude(do.call(rbind, test$mutations))
>
> while ./inst/doc/sequenza.R : genome.view(seg.cn <http://seg.cn> = seg.tab, info.type = "CNt")
> thus, seg.cn <http://seg.cn>  is assigned by seg.tab
> --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
> In R terminal, error comes after typing following
> sequenza2PyClone(mut.tab, seg.cn <http://seg.cn>=seg.tab, sample.id <http://sample.id>="TEST", norm.cn <http://norm.cn> = 2)
>
> “
> Error in `[.data.frame`(seg.cn <http://seg.cn>, i, c("CNt", "A", "B")) :
>   undefined columns selected
> "
>
> Hoping to hear from you
>
> Chong
>
> On Monday, June 20, 2016 at 5:37:18 PM UTC+8, Francesco Favero wrote:
> > Hi Chong He!
> > Thanks for trying this function. sequenza2PyClone was meant to be an experimental feature, I never tested it extensively.
> >
> > That’s the reason why sequenza2PyClone was not exported in the main namespace :). However you can still use the function by calling explicitly:
> >
> >    sequenza:::sequenza2PyClone
> >
> > This will just produce a data.frame with the .tsv required by pyclone, you still need to save with write.table…. (I hope the format is still the same, I didn’t test it with pyClone new releases.)
> >
> > You are welcome to write back if you have any issues with that.. or if the command still apply to current pyClone format..
> >
> > Best
> >
> > Francesco
> >
> >
> > > On 18 Jun 2016, at 07:10, Chong He <hecho...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > >
> > > Dear  all
> > >
> > > I am Chong HE from OEbiotech company China, and currently using Sequenza for tumor cellularity detection.
> > >
> > > As pyclone analysis needed, I ran sequenza2PyClone function in R terminal but found following :
> > >
> > > "Error: could not find function "sequenza2PyClone"
> > >
> > > There is sequenza2Pyclone function in next.R, but could not be called after library(sequenza), with little document about this function.
> > >
> > > We are curious about how to use this function
> > >
> > > Hoping to hear from you.
> > >
> > > ;-)
> > >
> > > Chong HE
